Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase. Zimbabwe players huddle out near the ropes. Max O'Dowd and Stephan Myburgh walk in with their blades for the Netherlands. Tendai Chatara comes to bowl. Here we go.
... The Run Chase ...

The conditions though are not that easy to bat on. Zimbabwe had struggled and so will the Netherlands. Which team will get over the line? To find out, do join us for the second essay in a short while.

Bas de Leede is in for a quick chat. He says it felts like the wicket was tough in the start and not as easy-paced as they expected but the bowlers did exceptionally well to restrict the opponents. Claims that he is happy that the injury was not serious. He credits the support staff who did all the tests and he is grateful to be able to play again. Ends by saying that with a small total they need one big partnership and two of their best can pull it off.

Netherlands were excellent with the ball. It was Paul van Meekeren who ran hovoc with the new ball and provided a great platform for the rest of his bowlers with his early wicket. He took three wickets. Logan van Beek, Bas de Leede and Brandon Glover took two each. They have managed to restrict Zimbabwe to a low total and now the onus is on their batters. They have their noses slightly ahead in this game at the inings break. They just need 118 to win this one.

The struggle continues with the blade for Zimbabwe. They started off on a bad note and lost three wickets inside the powerplay but the pair of Williams and Raza steadied the sinking ship. They played aggressively and were pouncing on anything loose. They lost Williams in the 12th over when a good partnership was brewing. Raza carried on but had an unlucky dismissal in the 15th over. He scored 40 off just 24 deliveries. If it wasn't for Raza, Zimbabwe would have been bowled out under a below-par total. Only two of the Zimbabwe batters managed to score in double digits!

OUT! CAUGHT! The Zimbabwe inning has been wrapped up and they will be really disappointed with their effort! Blessing Muzarabani is the last batter to be dismissed and Zimbabwe have their work cut out. Logan van Beek bangs this in short and wide outside off, Blessing Muzarabani looks to cut this but only manages to top edge this high into the sky. Brandon Glover is well-placed at backward point and he takes a comfortable catch to his teammates' delight. The Netherlands will be pumped with their effort in the field and will be confident of chasing this target.
Commentary.Howout: c Brandon Glover b Logan van Beek

Commentary.Commentary: Logan van Beek bowls a slower delivery on a good length and outside off, Tendai Chatara taps this towards short third man and takes a quick single.
Goes a touch fuller and gets the ball to nip back in sharply. Another inside edge into pads but no run this time.
Continues bowling on a good length and gets the ball to come back in. Tendai Chatara gets an inside edge onto his pads and they take a single as the ball rolls towards point.
This is on a good length and in line with the stumps, Tendai Chatara chips this over the bowler's head and takes a couple of runs.
Fuller one and on off, Tendai Chatara looks to play at it but misses.
This is fuller but still outside off, Blessing Muzarabani strokes this straight to cover and takes a quick single.
Bas de Leede bowls this on a good length and outside the off stump, Tendai Chatara guides this to short third man. A direct hit and an overthrow allows them to take a single.
This is on a good length and angling away from the right-hander. Blessing Muzarabani feels for this but is beaten.

OUT! CAUGHT! Richard Ngarava has fallen in his attempt to swing at every delivery! Fred Klaassen has quickly realized not to bowl on the pads and has stuck to the outside off stump line with this one being bowled a touch fuller. Richard Ngarava looks to go leg side though and gets a leading edge the goes high towards the point fielder. Stephan Myburgh takes a fine catch with both his hands over his head and Zimbabwe have just one wicket left.
Commentary.Howout: c Stephan Myburgh b Fred Klaassen

Commentary.Commentary: Blessing Muzarabani walks in.
WIDE! This is way beyond the tram line on the off side and Richard Ngarava leaves this one alone. The umpire calls this one wide.
Sticks to bowling on a good length but gets this one closer to the off stump, Richard Ngarava continues to swing wildly but does not get an bat on this one.
This is on a good length and outside the off pole, Richard Ngarava looks to cut this but gets an under edge towards the keeper.

SIX! This has been deposited into the stand well over any fielder! Fred Klaassen continues to bowl full on the pads, Richard Ngarava swings hard this time and connects well as the ball flies over the deep mid-wicket boundary for a maximum.

Fred Klaassen begins the over with a full delivery fired into the pads, Richard Ngarava clips this towards deep mid-wicket where the fielder does outstandingly well to dive and stop the ball. They take a couple of runs.
Short once again and on middle. Richard Ngarava looks to pull it but the ball hits his helmet. They cross for a leg bye.
Shorter one outside off, Tendai Chatara guides it to short third man for one.
This is on a good length and in line with the stumps, Tendai Chatara is watchful as hit taps this back down the pitch.
Tendai Chatara is the new batter.

OUT! CAUGHT! Zimbabwe are watching their chances fade away as the batters seem to be giving away their wickets cheaply! Bas de Leede bowls a slower delivery on a shorter length and outside the off stump, Luke Jongwe goes for the pull shot but is early into his shot. The ball flies high into the air and into the palms of Logan van Beek at mid-wicket. Zimbabwe are now eight down and staring down a barrel.
Commentary.Howout: c Logan van Beek b Bas de Leede

Commentary.Commentary: Goes 'round the wicket to the left-hander and serves this full into the stumps, Richard Ngarava hoicks this towards mid-wicket and takes a single.
Bas de Leede bowls this back of a length and outside off, Luke Jongwe pulls this uppishly towards long on and takes a single.
Richard Ngarava walks in.

OUT! BOWLED! Paul van Meekeren gets his third wicket in the final over of his spell and Zimbabwe are falling apart here! The bowler follows up a short ball with a full delivery just outside the off pole. Ryan Burl looks to drive but gets an inside edge that goes on to shatter the stumps. The Netherlands are right on top now as Zimbabwe lose their seventh wicket with 100 yet to be posted on the board.
Bangs this one short and pitching on leg stump. Ryan Burl ducks under this one and lets it through to the keeper.
Delivers this one a good length and outside the off stump, Ryan Burl swings his bat through the line but is beaten on the outside edge.
This is slightly short and outside off, Luke Jongwe gets on his backfoot and thumps this to deep point for a single.
Bowls this one short and angling down leg, Luke Jongwe pulls this to deep backward square leg and manages to pick up a couple of runs.
Paul van Meekeren bowls this full and outside the off stump, Luke Jongwe blocks this to the left of the bowler.
Good length, on off. Luke Jongwe knocks it to mid off for one again.
Slightly shorter again, this is again pulled towards mid-wicket for one.
Slightly shorter, on off. Luke Jongwe pulls it to mid-wicket for one.
Fuller and on off, Luke Jongwe pushes it to mid-wicket.
Luke Jongwe makes his way out to the crease now.

OUT! TAKEN! Excellent catch from Fred Klaassen and Netherlands finally get the danger man. Bowls it on a length and on the stumps, Raza stands still and lofts it but doesn't connect well. It goes high up in the air towards long on. Fred Klaassen settles under it but does not judge it well and eventually has to take it diving to his left. Sikandar Raza walks out after an amazing knock!
Commentary.Howout: c Fred Klaassen b Bas de Leede

Commentary.Commentary: A yorker and outside off, Sikandar Raza looks to play at it but misses.
Nails a yorker one leg, Sikandar Raza digs it to mid on for one.
FOUR! Fuller and just outside off, Sikandar Raza gets on his knee and smashes it past covers for a boundary!
Shorter one outside off, slower too. Sikandar Raza gets in two minds but leaves it alone in the end.
Length and on off, Ryan Burl pulls it to mid-wicket for one again.
Fuller and on off, Sikandar Raza looks to flick it but gets the upper part of his bat. It carries and falls just short of the fielder at mid-wicket. They collect one.
Looks like there will be a change of ball since there seems to be some damage on the previous one after hitting the stands. We are all set to resume now.
SIX! Up and over. On a length and on off, Sikandar Raza pulls it over deep mid-wicket for a maximum. That's a huge one from Sikandar Raza!
Wide! Slightly shorter and wide outside off, Sikandar Raza lets it go.
Slightly shorter and on middle, Ryan Burl looks to pull it but miscues it back towards the bowler.
Fuller one on off, Ryan Burl eases it towards the fielder at mid off.
Wide! Bangs a shorter one outside off, Ryan Burl lets it go. Wided.
Ryan Burl has made his way out to the crease.

OUT! TAKEN! Another one bites the dust. Bowls it fuller and on leg, Milton Shumba looks to play it with soft hands but mistimes it. It hits the upper part of his bat and carries towards short mid-wicket. Stephan Myburgh at short mid-wicket takes a dolly and Milton Shumba makes his way back into the hut.
Commentary.Howout: c Stephan Myburgh b Logan van Beek

Commentary.Commentary: Serves it outside off, Milton Shumba cuts it towards deep point for a brace.
Fuller and on off, Sikandar Raza drills it to long off for one.
SIX! Bang! Sikandar Raza connects and connects well. On a length and on off, Sikandar Raza plays a hook shot over deep mid-wicket for a biggie.
Full and on leg, Milton Shumba defends it back towards the bowler.
Milton Shumba makes his way out ot the middle.

OUT! TAKEN! Zimbabwe lose their fourth and the partnership is broken. Slightly shorter and on off, Sean Williams pulls it but doesn't connect well. The ball goes up in the air and towards deep mid-wicket. Max O'Dowd settles under it and pouches it safely. The partnership was looking a bit threatening but has finally come to an end.
Commentary.Howout: c Max O'Dowd b Paul van Meekeren

Commentary.Commentary: Good length again, on leg. Sikandar Raza knocks it to mid on for one.
FOUR! Excellent timing. On a length and on off, Sikandar Raza stands firm and slaps it past covers for a boundary!
Slightly shorter and outside off, Sean Williams taps it to point for one.
Fuller one drifting down leg side, Sikandar Raza looks to flick it but gets his pads. They cross for a leg bye.
Nice and full again, on leg. Sikandar Raza works it to mid-wicket for one.
Fuller one, on middle. Sikandar Raza digs it back towards Roelof van der Merwe. Good bowling.
Fuller one on middle, Sean Williams eases it to mid on for a quick single. Good running!
Outside off this time, Sean Williams looks to flick it but gets an outside edge. The ball rolls towards third man. They collect two.
FOUR! Well connected this time. bowls it on middle, Sean Williams reverse sweeps through backward point for a boundary!
Tossed up, outside off. Sean Williams looks to cut it but misses.

Drinks! The game sits in balance at the halfway stage of the first innings. The Netherlands were off to a flying start and bagged some early wickets inside the powerplay. Sikandar Raza and Sean Williams now have managed to gather some momentum and they would hope to continue with their partnership. The scoreboard reads 53/3 at the halfway stage.
Goes 'round the wicket to the southpaw and bangs this in short outside off, Sean Williams gets on top of the bounce and pulls the ball towards deep square leg to take a single to retain strike.
Delivers this a touch fuller and attacks the stumps once again. Sikandar Raza taps this towards mid on and takes a quick single.
This one is on a good length and in line with the stumps, Sikandar Raza flicks this towards short mid-wicket.
Continues bowling full and outside off to the right-hander. Sikandar Raza punches this to the right of mid off.
Goes full this time and into the pads, Sean Williams clips this to deep square leg and collects a single.
Bas de Leede bowls this full and outside off, Sean Williams strokes this straight to the mid off fielder.
This is short as well and outside off, Sikandar Raza shimmies forward and swings hard but does not connect this time. A really good over for Zimbabwe as 12 runs have come off it.

Little bit of luck here for Sikandar Raza! Brandon Glover goes back to bowling full and outside off, Sikandar Raza swings his bat and gets a leading edge that falls in the vacant deep point region. They take a couple of runs.

SIX! This has been swatted away! Brandon Glover bangs this in short but the ball does not rise up as much and sits up nicely for Sikandar Raza to pull this over the deep square leg boundary for a biggie. He has played this shot completely off balance but has still managed to find the elevation and distance.

FOUR! Sikandar Raza looking to be aggressive now! Brandon Glover bowls this full and outside the off stump, Sikandar Raza does not connect this cleanly but manages to clear the infield fielder and find the long off fence for four more runs.
Offers width this time and serves this on a good length, Sikandar Raza rocks back in the crease and thumps this to deep cover for a brace.
Brandon Glover bowls this on a good length and gets the ball to move back into the batter. Sikandar Raza defends this to the leg side.

FOUR! This has been crunched away! Logan van Beek goes full this time and wide outside off, Sean Williams strokes this through covers with very little foot movement and finds the deep cover fence for four runs.
This is on a good length and outside off, Sean Williams is watchful as he taps this to the point fielder.
Pulls his length back and serves this outside off, Sean Williams slaps this to wide deep point and collects two runs for himself.
Goes full this time but still outside the off pole, Sean Williams gets his front foot forward and strokes the ball straight to mid off. The dot ball count is increasing for Zimbabwe.
Bowls this one on a good length and outside the off stump, Sean Williams blocks this towards point.
Logan van Beek begins with a back-of-a-length delivery served wide outside off, Sean Williams mistimes his slash towards the cover fielder.
Continues bowling on a good length but gets this one to nip back in sharply. Hits the back pad of the batter and the bowler seems interested but it looks like there was a bit on an inside edge.
WIDE! This is on a good length but straying down leg side. The umpire calls this one wide.

Goes full this time and outside the off stump, Sean Williams strokes this straight to mid off and takes off for a quick single. There is a direct hit at the striker's end and they go upstairs to check but the batter has made it across the crease.
Bowls this one a fraction short and outside off, Sean Williams goes for the pull shot but does not time this well but they get a couple of runs.
This is on a good length and gets the ball to nip back in after pitching on leg, Sean Williams looks to make room but gets cramped for space.
Back of a length again, Sean Williams pulls it to deep mid-wicket for a brace.
FOUR! Slightly shorter and on off, Sean Williams pulls it through square leg for a boundary!
Sikandar Raza is the new batter.

OUT! PLUMB! Brandon Glover gets the wicket he deserves! He has had two catches dropped this over and in the end, he claims the wicket himself! After bothering the batter with out swinging deliveries he gets one to nip back in from a fuller length and just outside off. Regis Chakabva is playing for the movement away and gets rapped on the pads. The umpire raises his finger and the batter does not choose to review as he knows he is a goner. Zimbabwe have now lost three wickets and are in some serious trouble as they are 20 for 3 after the Powerplay.
This is on a good length as well and moving away from outside off, Regis Chakabva is watchful now as he leaves this one alone as well.
On a length and outside off, Regis Chakabva leaves it alone.

DROPPED ONCE AGAIN! The Netherlands are letting opportunities go here! Brandon Glover serves this on a good length and outside off, Regis Chakabva swings at this and gets a thick edge that goes to the right of the keeper. Scott Edwards is the culprit this time as he is unable to pouch this despite having the gloves on.

DROPPED! A chance goes begging here! Brandon Glover bowls this slightly short and outside the off stump, Regis Chakabva gets in position and slaps the ball straight to the point fielder. Bas de Leede does not have to move but the ball enters his palms and pops out. What a chance!
WIDE! This is well outside off beyond the tram line. Regis Chakabva leaves this one alone and the umpire calls this wide.

Brandon Glover bowls from 'round the wicket to the left-hander and angles this into the pads on a good length. Sean Williams misses his flick and the ball rolls to square leg off the pads and they take a leg bye.
Fuller one down leg, Regis Chakabva looks to flick it but gets his pads. A half-hearted appeal from the bowler but turned down by the umpire.
This is on a good length and outside the off stump, Regis Chakabva is surprised by the extra bounce but manages to defend the ball to the right of the bowler.
Bowls this on in line with the stumps on a fuller length, Regis Chakabva flicks the ball towards short mid-wicket.
Fuller delivery on the pads, Sean Williams flicks it nicely to wide of mid on for three runs.
Back of a length and outside off, Sean Williams leaves it alone.
Fuller one on off, Regis Chakabva looks to play at it but gets a thick outside edge over backward point for a single. Falls well short of third man fielder.
Sean Williams the half-centurion from their last game makes his way out to the middle.

OUT! CAUGHT! What an end to an over from Brandon Glover. A wicket-maiden and Craig Ervine makes his way back into the hut. Brandon Glover angles it on the stumps, Craig Ervine was feeling the pressure and he tries to flick it onto the leg side but mistimes it completely. Scott Edwards settles under it and takes a fine catch.
Commentary.Howout: c Scott Edwards b Brandon Glover

Commentary.Commentary: Another fuller one, this one nips in a long way. Craig Ervine looks to play at it but the ball hits his thigh. Five dots now!
Four dots in a row. Fuller and on off, Craig Ervine knocks it towards the fielder at mid on.
Good-length delivery, on off. Craig Ervine blocks it back towards the bowler.
Serves it outside off, Craig Ervine cuts it but finds the fielder at backward point. Good fielding!
On a length and on leg, Craig Ervine eases it straight towards the mid on fielder.
Make it four dots. Fuller one, on off. Regis Chakabva defends it solidly. Another fine over from the Netherlands!
This one lands down leg, Regis Chakabva looks to flick it but doesn't connect well. Three dots now.
On a length and on off, Regis Chakabva defends it back towards the bowler. Another dot.
Good length and down middle, Regis Chakabva awkwardly defends it away.
An outswinger again, Craig Ervine looks to play at it but gets an outside edge towards third man. They collect one.
On a length and outside off, this is left alone by Craig Ervine.
FOUR! This one lands just outside off, Regis Chakabva looks to loft it but gets a thick outside edge. The ball goes over the slips and races away the third man fence. Lucky boundary!
Another length ball outside off, Regis Chakabva leaves it alone. Another dot.
On a length and outside off, Regis Chakabva lets it go.
Regis Chakabva makes his way out to the middle at number 3.

OUT! TIMBER! The Netherlands have drawn first blood and Zimbabwe's opening woes continue! Bowls it touch fuller, it swings in a bit. Wesley Madhevere looks to flick it but completely misses it as the ball rattles the middle pole. The Netherlands have an early breakthrough in the game. Wesley Madhevere departs for one and Zimbabwe need to build a partnership here.
Bowls it outside off, Craig Ervine cuts it towards short third man. The fielder stops it well diving to his left. They cross.
Another one down leg, Craig Ervine looks to flick it but the ball brushes his pads and is collected by the keeper diving to his right.

FIVE WIDES! Expensive start to the second over. This one lands outside leg, Craig Ervine looks to flick it but misses. The keeper misses it as well as the ball races away the fine leg fence for five extra runs as the umpire indicates that this is wide.
Paul van Meekeren will share the attack and bowl from the other end.
Back of a length and on the stumps, Wesley Madhevere defends it straight back to the bowler. Good start from Fred Klaassen. Just three coming off the opening over.
Another outswinger and Craig Ervine looks to defend it with soft hands but gets an outside edge down the third man region for a single.
Oh, that was close. Bowls it just outside off swinging it away from the batter, Craig Ervine looks to defend it but misses.
Touch fuller this time, on off. Wesley Madhevere knocks it to mid off for one.
Wide! This one lands wide outside off, Wesley Madhevere leaves it alone and is called wide by the umpire.
Another one just outside off, this one nips in a bit. Wesley Madhevere fends it to point.
Fred Klaassen starts with a length ball outside off, Wesley Madhevere lets it go. A dot to start with.

We are all set for the game to begin after the pre-match formalities as the umpires make their way out to the pitch. The players of the Netherlands form a huddle before taking their respective positions in the field as Wesley Madhevere and Craig Ervine stride onto the ground to open the innings for Zimbabwe. They will be looking to get their team off to a good start in this game and set a platform for their team. Fred Klaassen has been handed the new ball and he will begin proceedings. Let's play...

We are moments away from the start of the game but before that the umpires and players have lined up in the middle for the national anthems. It will be the national anthem of the Netherlands first followed by Zimbabwe's national anthem.

PITCH REPORT - Mpumelelo Mbangwa is pitchside and he says that the weather is wonderful and mentions that the ground is a perfect oval. Adds that the square boundaries are short whereas the straight boundaries are much longer. He is joined by Dirk Nannes who informs that the Adelaide pitch is hairy as it has a lot of grass. Claims that it is a very firm pitch therefore the grass should not be a worry as the ground is hard. Ends by saying that batting first or chasing, both should not be an issue.

Scott Edwards the skipper of the Netherlands says that they were going to bowl anyways. Adds that the wickets were under covers so they would hope to restrict their opponents to a small total. Ends by saying that they still have two games to go and they are looking to win this one.

Craig Ervine the skipper of Zimbabwe says that they are looking to bat first as it is sunny and the pitch may not change much. Adds that they are looking to put a decent score on the board and defend it. Admits that the start has been an issue for them and they have been losing a cluster of wickets. Mentions that they want to access the new conditions at a new venue and not lose too many wickets. Informs that they have one change as Brad Evans has picked up a slight niggle.

Netherlands (Playing XI) - Max O'Dowd, Stephan Myburgh, Tom Cooper, Colin Ackermann, Bas de Leede, Scott Edwards (C/WK), Roelof van der Merwe, Logan van Beek (In for Tim Pringle), Fred Klaassen, Paul van Meekeren, Brandon Glover.

Zimbabwe (Playing XI) - Wesley Madhevere, Craig Ervine (C), Milton Shumba, Sean Williams, Sikandar Raza, Regis Chakabva (WK), Ryan Burl, Luke Jongwe (In for Brad Evans), Tendai Chatara, Richard Ngarava, Blessing Muzarabani.
TOSS - The coin lands in favor of Zimbabwe. They will BAT first.

Scott Edwards' team will be trying for a comeback in this game. The Netherlands never appeared to be in a good position in any of their previous matches. They came close to a win over Bangladesh in their first game but were completely outplayed in their subsequent matches against India and Pakistan. The only positive for the Netherlands was the 4 wickets they bagged against Pakistan while defending a low total. The batting order has the tendency to collapse from decent positions but this game will be a great opportunity for them to register their first win in the Super 12 stage. Which team will be more motivated to come out on top? Let's find out soon. Stay tuned for the toss and team updates.
